entities.summary:
Lodovico (Ludovico) Calini (1696–1782) was an Italian cardinal from Brescia whose career bridged pastoral episcopacy and late-Ancien Régime curial service. Elevated to the cardinalate in the eighteenth century, he belonged to the Lombard clerical elite that staffed northern Italian sees while remaining tied to Rome’s congregations and ceremonial calendar.

Calini’s long life stretched across Benedict XIV’s learned papacy, the suppression crises of the Jesuits, and the early reformist currents that preceded Josephinism. As a cardinal from Venetian Lombardy he navigated overlapping jurisdictions—Brescia’s civic Catholicism, Venetian political oversight, and papal authority—typical of northern Italian church government.

He is remembered chiefly as a stable institutional figure rather than a doctrinal celebrity: an example of how provincial noble clergy still reached the Sacred College in the century before revolutionary upheaval dismantled the old ecclesiastical order.
